name: ElevenLabs
summary: AI voice platform with hyper-realistic text-to-speech (Eleven v4 and the low-latency v4 Turbo since September 2026), voice cloning, dubbing, sound effects and conversational agents. It also has a developer API and, since August 2026, a hosted MCP connector that runs inside Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor. Free tier to test voices before you pay.
best_for: creators, developers and product teams that want the most realistic AI voices available: voiceovers, audiobooks, dubbing, conversational agents and a well-documented API
skip_if: you generate hours of long-form audio on a tight budget (credit math punishes volume: flat-hour tools or the TTS built into your video editor may be enough), or you need acted emotional range only a human voice actor delivers
honest_knock: Credits are the meter and retakes are the tax: you are charged per generation request, and a regeneration is only free while the content and settings are unchanged, so real usage lands well above the calculator estimate. And read the free-tier fine print: $0 gets you 10k credits to play with, but no commercial license: anything you publish commercially needs at least the $6 Starter. Voice realism leads the market; niche names and jargon can still need manual retakes, so run your hardest paragraph through the free tier before subscribing.

pricing.notes:
(re-verified 23 Nov 2026 on elevenlabs.io/pricing) Every plan rate held again, unchanged since August. Free $0 with 10k credits/mo; Starter $6/mo (30k credits, commercial license; on 23 November 2026 the card still advertised the first month at $1, while the site banner for that offer still read "Ends September 30"); Creator $22/mo — first month 50% off at $11 — with ~121k credits. Then Pro $99/mo (~600k credits, 44.1kHz PCM), Scale $299/mo (~1.8M credits, 3 workspace seats) and Business $990/mo (~6M credits, 10 seats). Extra usage runs roughly $0.36 down to $0.17 per additional minute depending on tier.

Two things the plan cards do not put next to the price. Annual billing is sold as ten months rather than twelve — the FAQ writes it out as annual price = monthly price × 10, which works out to $5 for Starter, $18.33 for Creator, $82.50 for Pro, $249.17 for Scale and $825 for Business. And credits are shared across every product, so speech, music, dubbing and video all draw down the same monthly balance. On a paid plan unused credits roll over for up to two months — the balance caps at three times the monthly quota — but downgrading or cancelling forfeits whatever is left at the end of the cycle, and the free plan has no rollover at all. Pay-as-you-go top-up credits sit outside that rollover cap, and upgrading carries unused credits into the next cycle. The FAQ now lists what the shared pool costs per product: text to speech 1 credit per character, speech to text 330 credits a minute, music 900 a minute, voice changer and isolator 1,000 a minute, sound effects 200 per generation, and dubbing 2,000 to 10,000 credits a minute depending on watermark and Studio.

Historical: a launch offer ran until 12 October 2026 (read 30 September 2026 on elevenlabs.io/pricing/api and the Eleven v4 launch post): API text to speech on Eleven v4 is $0.022 per 1,000 characters instead of $0.08, and on Eleven v4 Turbo $0.011 instead of $0.04, 72% off; the site banner also offers 3x credits on Creator and above until the same date. It ended on 12 October; the pricing page read on 30 October 2026 no longer carries it, and the list rates apply.

Black Friday, read 23 November 2026: the pricing FAQ says the sale "ends on December 1st" and that until then eligible customers "can save up to 55% when they choose an annual plan". It applies to the first year of the Creator and Pro annual plans. "Creator annual costs $99 for the year", against $220 at the normal ten-months-for-twelve rate, which is the 55% the banner claims. Pro newcomers get the full 55%; people already paying monthly for Pro get 50% off if they move to annual billing.

sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 15 November 2026 the session tested ElevenLabs on the free plan: the onboarding, what 500 characters cost in credits, how fast the audio starts, the commercial license on the free plan, the checkout of the cheapest paid plan up to the card form and the way to delete the account. Nothing was paid or deleted. A test text of exactly 500 characters (English, with the numbers 2026, 15 and 67) was entered; the counter said 10,000 credits remaining and 500 / 10,000 characters. Generate speech was clicked at 17:53:13 with the default voice Roger and the model Eleven v4. After about 7 seconds, at 17:53:20, audio was already playing. Each click produced two versions, Generation 1 and Generation 2, and the player showed a length of 0:39. Afterwards the account menu showed Remaining 9,500: 500 characters cost exactly 500 credits, even though two versions came out. By the tester arithmetic, 10,000 credits a month is about 20 such paragraphs, roughly 13 minutes of speech (20 times 39 seconds). After generating, the panel Recommended for your text proposed other voices. The voice quality was not formally assessed and nothing is claimed about it. No kit records were entered.
findings: A test text of exactly 500 characters was voiced on the free plan with the default voice Roger and the model Eleven v4. Generate speech was clicked at 17:53:13 and audio played at 17:53:20, about 7 seconds later. Each click produced two versions of 0:39.

The balance went from 10,000 to 9,500 credits, so 500 characters cost exactly 500 credits even though two versions came out. At that rate the 10,000 free credits a month cover about 20 such paragraphs, roughly 13 minutes of speech (our arithmetic).
On the free plan the Commercial license for Speech and Music is crossed out. Starter adds it, together with Instant Voice Cloning and the dubbing studio.

The Starter checkout in euros showed 1.14 euros due today including 0.20 euros VAT (promo for the first month), then 6.85 euros a month. Before that, a window offered annual billing with 2 months free. We stopped before the card details.
The onboarding has a required checkbox confirming you are 18 or older, which the account owner has to tick.

Settings, Profile, Delete Entire Account says you can no longer create an ElevenLabs account with this email, so deleting the account blocks that address for good. We did not press it. We did not judge voice quality.
not_tested: We did not watch the original sign-up; the account was already open when our session began.
We skipped voice cloning on purpose, and did not try Studio, Dubbing, Music, the API, downloading or reusing the audio, or any paid plan.
We did not judge how good the voice sounds.
We did not contact support, invite anyone, enter card details, or export and re-import data.
The account deletion, which blocks the email address for good, is left to the account owner.
Session date 15 November 2026, Europe/Amsterdam time. Our clock readings are approximate and not a benchmark.
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
